This site teaches the code behind a published study by translating the original Stata analysis into R, step by step. The paper is @hemmige2018str.

## Clinical background

Single-tablet regimens (STRs) combine a complete antiretroviral regimen in one pill taken once a day. When the study was done, the only first-line STR in wide use at the clinic was efavirenz/tenofovir/emtricitabine (Atripla); the usual alternatives were a ritonavir-boosted protease inhibitor (darunavir or atazanavir) taken with tenofovir/emtricitabine (Truvada), which was three or four pills once a day. The question was whether starting on one pill rather than three or four went with staying in care and reaching viral suppression in the first year. More on the [clinical background](quarto/background.qmd) page.

## What this analysis does

It uses pharmacy fills, CD4 counts and viral loads from Thomas Street Health Center, a Harris Health System safety-net HIV clinic in Houston, for patients starting antiretroviral therapy (ART) in 2008-2011. It compares patients who started Atripla with those who started a boosted protease inhibitor with Truvada, on retention in care, viral suppression at least once in the first year, and medication coverage. It is an observational study: the comparison is weighted for measured differences between the groups, not randomized.

## Methods

Every patient becomes one row per day from 2008 to 2013, and each day records the regimen, whether pills were on hand, and the most recent labs. Outcomes are then compared between the two groups with and without inverse probability of treatment weights from a propensity score. [Study design and methods](quarto/study_methods.qmd) explains each step in plain language, and the [analysis plan](quarto/analysis-plan.qmd) is the formal specification.

## How to use this site

- **Code** pages follow the R scripts in the order `R/main.R` runs them. Each one explains a step and shows the R code next to the Stata it replaces.
- **Original Stata code** shows the do-files behind the paper as they were, with patient-level details removed, and how they fit together.

## Terms used on this site

- **ART:** antiretroviral therapy.
- **STR / MTR:** single-tablet regimen / multi-tablet regimen.
- **Viral suppression:** a viral load at or below the threshold, here 400 copies/mL. "Suppressed in year one" means at least once in the first year, not throughout it.
- **Retention in care:** at least two viral load tests in the first year, more than 90 days apart; an adaptation of the HRSA (Health Resources and Services Administration) HIV/AIDS Bureau measure ("HRSA-style").
- **PDC:** proportion of days covered: the share of days on which a patient had every drug of the regimen on hand, by the pharmacy record.
- **Propensity score:** the estimated probability that a patient like this one started the STR.
- **IPW / IPTW:** inverse probability (of treatment) weighting; see [Inverse probability weighting](quarto/ipw.qmd).
- **ATE:** average treatment effect: the comparison of everyone in the cohort starting one regimen against everyone starting the other.
- **Intention to treat:** patients stay in the group of the regimen they started, even if they switch.
- **LVCF:** last value carried forward: each day takes the most recent test result.

[Braces](https://forum.posit.co/t/curly-braces-around-package-name-convention/122547) identify R packages throughout this site.

## Status

Teaching material for a completed, published study. The R code has been run only on synthetic data; it has not been used to reproduce the published numbers, and no real data or results from it are in this repository.
